scope: UK Skilled Worker sponsor duties and sponsor change-impact preflight only

rules.proposition: Report specified sponsored-worker changes generally within 10 working days.
Report unauthorised absence exceeding 10 consecutive working days.

Report new normal work locations including a new branch/client site or permanent/full-time home working; hybrid-only or occasional day-to-day changes need not be reported when the main office is unchanged.
Report when sponsorship ends or the worker no longer requires sponsorship for specified reasons.
Report significant sponsor-organisation changes generally within 20 working days.

rules.locator: C4 mergers, takeovers and similar changes
rules.proposition: Mergers, takeovers and TUPE transfers have sponsor-licence and reporting consequences; certain same-job transfers need no new CoS if the receiving sponsor has the relevant licence.
A sponsored worker should generally start no later than 28 days after the relevant start-date trigger; after that the sponsor must report the new start/reason or stop sponsorship.
Unpaid or reduced-pay absence over 4 weeks in total generally requires sponsorship to stop unless a permitted exception or accepted compelling reason applies.
Listed exceptions include statutory family leave, sick leave, humanitarian crisis, industrial action, jury service and court-witness absence; extended absence remains reportable.

Same-occupation eligible changes can normally continue with reporting; different occupation-code changes generally require a new CoS and approved change-of-employment application before the new job starts.

A salary reduction may be report-only if the same salary option remains met, may require a new CoS/application if another Skilled Worker salary basis remains available, or may require sponsorship to stop if salary requirements are no longer met.
Sponsors must retain prescribed records and evidence supporting sponsored-worker compliance.
